## Exact baseline provenance

The baseline squared voltage is `v_j^0 = abs2(primary_voltage_complex_pu[j])` from one corrected fixed-injection AC solve at `P13_VPP=P30_VPP=0`. The production data path is `run_analytical_audit -> default_baseline_evaluator -> AxisScan.evaluate_fixed_injection -> Stage0.evaluate_point -> Stage0.assemble_stage0_inputs -> Stage0.primary_power_flow`. The assembly reads the canonical timestamp's load multiplier and PV factor, places `850*f_t` kW of reference PV at bus 13, applies zero VPP injection at buses 13 and 30, scales the canonical active and reactive loads, converts net demand on the 10,000-kW base, and solves the radial AC equations. The primary phasors—not the replay voltage vector and not a flat classical-LinDistFlow baseline—supply `v_j^0`.

At this timestamp, `f_t=0.914956873902116`, reference PV is `777.713342816799 kW`, and the load multiplier is `0.155940374398887`.

## Bus-13/bus-30 candidate intersection

The coefficient matrix in squared-voltage per per-unit power is `[0.893822890071851 0.268450094711859; 0.268450094711859 0.625073311221421]`; its determinant is `0.486639380191906` and 2-norm condition number is `2.30737830364874` (threshold `10000000000`).

The equality intersection is `P13*=156.89470053622 kW`, `P30*=1610.27566755161 kW`; both coordinates are strictly positive: `true`. Normalized equality residuals are `1.21200268545942e-16` and `0`.

The selected-line intercept inequalities are `L(13,13)<L(30,13): true` and `L(30,30)<L(13,30): true`. Together with nonnegative coefficients and a nonsingular, well-conditioned matrix, the opposite intercept ordering places the two selected-line intersection in the open positive quadrant.
